definitions.definition: (intransitive) To form an agreement or contract.

quote.text: In return for the sovereign's protection, they compacted to police the content of public literature.

quote.text: O Gorice XI., most glorious King of Witchland, and O Lord Goldry Bluszco, captain of the hosts of Demonland, it is compact betwixt you, and made fast by mighty oaths whereof I, the Red Foliot, am keeper, that ye shall wrastle three falls together on these conditions,  […]

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French compact, from Latin compāctus, perfect passive participle of compingō (“join together”), from com- (“together”) + pangō (“fasten”), from Proto-Indo-European *pag- (“to fasten”).

definitions.definition: Closely packed or densely constituted; having much material in a small volume.

quote.text: glass, crystal, gems, and other compact bodies

definitions.definition: Having all necessary features fitting neatly into a small space.
(of prose) Brief and pithy; not verbose.

Such that every open cover has a finite subcover. In a metric space, this is equivalent to being sequentially compact. In metric spaces with the Heine-Borel property, this is equivalent to being closed and bounded.
Compact in the above sense and moreover Hausdorff.
(topology, not comparable) Of a topological space:
(obsolete) Joined or held together; leagued; confederated.

definitions.definition: A slim folding case, often featuring a mirror, powder and a powder puff, small enough to fit in a woman's purse, handbag, or pocket.
An automobile that is larger than a subcompact but smaller than an intermediate.
A broadsheet newspaper published in the size of a tabloid but keeping its non-sensational style.

quote.citation: 2012, BBC News, Dundee Courier makes move to compact‎[5]:
quote.text: The Dundee Courier has announced the newspaper will be relaunching as a compact later this week. Editor Richard Neville said a "brighter, bolder" paper would appear from Saturday, shrunk from broadsheet to tabloid size.
